attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter, stated as his own view.

semantics.note: Present-tense observation. The exclusion of Anthropic and OpenAI compute spend is kept. 'No real sign' plus 'explosion' is a firm claim that no evidence exists.

contract.note: Reading 'explosion' as very rapid realized growth, with one clear counterexample enough, is an ordinary plain reading. The surrounding text suggests he may have meant scale relative to capex ('OpenAI-sized chunks'), so the result depends on that reading, and the contract flags this.

evidence.note: Alphabet's Q1 2026 letter, published 2026-04-29, before the post: revenue from products built on its own gen AI models grew nearly 800% YoY. These are first-party model products, not Anthropic or OpenAI compute purchases. It is a company disclosure and gives no absolute revenue.

reviews.rationale: Before the post, Google publicly reported nearly 800% YoY Q1 2026 revenue growth for products built on its own gen AI models. That is a visible sign of explosive AI revenue growth outside the excluded lab compute spend. Absolute size is not disclosed, and it is a company statement, but under the contract's plain reading it is a clear counterexample to 'no real sign'.

attribution.note: Zitron's own projection in his newsletter.

semantics.note: 'On course to spend at least $7M' is a firm trajectory forecast and can be scored. The $10M figure is hedged ('might') and is not scored. The 'nearly half of net income' comparison belongs to the $10M case, so the proposition attaches it loosely, but the scored core is intact.

contract.note: Scoring only the $7M minimum, on AI-service and token spending for calendar 2026, matches the context. It fairly treats $10M as a possibility rather than a threshold.

evidence.note: Zillow's FY2025 release confirms the $23M GAAP net income used as the comparison base. It covers a different period and metric, so it says nothing about 2026 AI spending.

reviews.rationale: The deadline is the end of calendar 2026, after the 2026-10-28 evaluation date. The packet has no verified cumulative 2026 spending of $7M or more, so the early-resolution rule is not met. Spending staying below the threshold so far is not failure. The forecast cannot be scored yet.
